title: CVS Health Announces Major Plan to Split Its Business
subtitle: The healthcare giant will separate its pharmacy chain from its insurance and benefits operations by 2028.

summary.en: CVS Health has announced plans to divide its massive company into two separate businesses. The move will separate its retail pharmacies from its insurance and benefits divisions. This decision follows growing pressure from lawmakers who worry that large healthcare companies have become too powerful. Many believe these large corporations have caused medical costs to rise for the average person. The company hopes this change will make healthcare more affordable and easier for patients to use.
summary.zh: CVS 健康宣布計畫將其龐大的公司拆分為兩家獨立的企業。此舉將把零售藥局業務與保險及福利部門分開。這項決定是在立法者日益擔憂大型醫療保健公司權力過大後所做出的。許多人認為，這些大型企業已導致一般民眾的醫療成本上升。該公司希望此項變革能使醫療保健更實惠，並讓病患使用起來更方便。

paragraphs.en: CVS Health, one of the largest healthcare companies in the United States, has announced a major change to its business structure. The company, which is worth $117 billion, plans to split its operations into two separate businesses. This decision marks the end of a period where healthcare companies grew into massive conglomerates—large groups of companies that own many different types of businesses. According to The Guardian Business, this change is expected to be completed by early 2028.
paragraphs.zh: 美國最大的醫療保健公司之一 CVS 健康 (CVS Health) 宣布其商業結構將有重大變革。這家市值達 1170 億美元的公司計畫將業務拆分為兩家獨立的企業。此項決定象徵著醫療保健公司擴張成為龐大企業集團——即擁有許多不同類型業務的大型公司組合——的時代告一段落。根據《衛報商業版》(The Guardian Business) 報導，這項變革預計將於 2028 年初完成。

paragraphs.en: Under the new plan, the first company will be called CVS Pharmacy. It will include the company’s 9,000 retail stores, in-store clinics, and mail-order prescription services. The second company will keep the name CVS Health. This part of the business will manage the insurance provider Aetna and a large pharmacy benefits manager called Caremark. It will also include services that provide home visits and primary care for older people. David Joyner, the current chief executive and chair of CVS, will lead this healthcare solutions business.
paragraphs.zh: 根據新計畫，第一家公司將命名為 CVS 藥局 (CVS Pharmacy)。它將涵蓋該公司旗下的 9000 家零售門市、店內診所及郵購處方藥服務。第二家公司將保留 CVS 健康的名稱。這部分業務將管理保險供應商安泰保險 (Aetna) 以及名為 Caremark 的大型藥品福利管理機構。它也將包含為老年人提供居家訪視與初級照護的服務。現任 CVS 執行長兼董事長大衛·喬伊納 (David Joyner) 將領導這家醫療保健解決方案公司。

paragraphs.en: This announcement follows years of rapid growth for CVS Health. The company began expanding into almost every part of the healthcare system in 2018, when it completed a $70 billion deal to buy Aetna. Other large healthcare rivals, such as UnitedHealth Group and Cigna, followed similar strategies. By bringing insurance, pharmacy benefits, and retail services under one roof, these companies hoped to control more of the market. However, The Guardian Business reports that these three companies now control about 80% of the market, which has led to significant concern among government officials.
paragraphs.zh: 這項公告是在 CVS 健康經歷多年快速成長後發布的。該公司自 2018 年以 700 億美元收購安泰保險並完成交易後，便開始擴張至醫療保健系統的幾乎每個環節。其他大型醫療保健競爭對手，如聯合健康集團 (UnitedHealth Group) 與信諾集團 (Cigna)，也採取了類似策略。透過將保險、藥品福利與零售服務整合在同一屋簷下，這些公司希望掌控更多市場。然而，《衛報商業版》報導指出，這三家公司目前已控制了約 80% 的市場，這已引起政府官員的高度擔憂。

paragraphs.en: Lawmakers and regulators have put increasing pressure on these healthcare giants. Many argue that these companies have become too dominant, which has led to higher medical costs for patients. In response, some states have already taken action. For example, Arkansas and Tennessee have passed laws to prevent companies from managing prescription benefits while also running retail and mail-order pharmacies. Other states are currently considering similar rules to limit the power of these large corporations.
paragraphs.zh: 立法者與監管機構對這些醫療保健巨頭施加了越來越大的壓力。許多人認為，這些公司已變得過於強勢，導致病患的醫療成本上升。作為回應，一些州已經採取行動。例如，阿肯色州與田納西州已通過法律，禁止公司在經營零售與郵購藥局的同時，又管理處方藥福利。其他州目前也正在考慮制定類似規則，以限制這些大型企業的權力。

paragraphs.en: At the federal level, there is also a push for change. Senators Josh Hawley and Elizabeth Warren have introduced a bill that proposes an antitrust crackdown—a set of government actions designed to stop companies from becoming monopolies that control too much of an industry. Senator Hawley stated that this legislation is a major step toward making healthcare more transparent and affordable for every American. The Guardian Business noted that this political pushback against healthcare giants has been a significant factor in the company's decision.
paragraphs.zh: 在聯邦層級，推動變革的呼聲也日益高漲。參議員喬許·霍利 (Josh Hawley) 與伊莉莎白·華倫 (Elizabeth Warren) 提出了一項法案，提議進行反壟斷打擊——這是一系列旨在阻止公司成為壟斷整個產業的政府行動。霍利參議員表示，這項立法是讓醫療保健對每位美國人而言更透明、更實惠的重要一步。據《衛報商業版》指出，這種針對醫療保健巨頭的政治反彈，是該公司做出此項決定的重要因素。

paragraphs.en: This move represents a major change in strategy for CVS Health. Previously, the company strongly opposed legislative efforts to break up its business. A company spokesman had even warned that such a breakup could allow private equity firms to strip the healthcare system for parts. However, the company has faced challenges in meeting the growth expectations of its investors. In late 2024, the company's share price fell to $44, although it has since recovered.
paragraphs.zh: 此舉代表 CVS 健康在策略上的重大轉變。先前，該公司強烈反對任何拆分業務的立法努力。公司發言人甚至曾警告，此類拆分可能會讓私募股權公司有機會將醫療保健系統拆解變賣。然而，該公司在滿足投資人的成長預期方面面臨挑戰。2024 年底，該公司股價一度跌至 44 美元，儘管隨後已有所回升。

paragraphs.en: In a statement regarding the split, David Joyner explained that the company’s history is defined by changing to stay ahead of the future. He noted that in today’s environment, the company needs to deliver more affordability, better access, and a simpler experience for patients. By separating the pharmacy chain from the insurance and benefits business, CVS Health hopes to address these needs more effectively.
paragraphs.zh: 在關於拆分的聲明中，大衛·喬伊納解釋說，該公司的歷史是由為了在未來保持領先而進行的變革所定義的。他指出，在當今的環境下，公司需要為病患提供更高的負擔能力、更好的取得管道以及更簡便的體驗。透過將藥局連鎖店與保險及福利業務分離，CVS 健康希望更有效地滿足這些需求。

paragraphs.en: As the company prepares for this transition, the healthcare industry is watching closely. The move reflects a broader national debate about the size and influence of large healthcare corporations. Whether this split will lead to lower prices and better service for the public remains to be seen, but it is clear that the era of the massive healthcare conglomerate is facing new challenges. For now, CVS Health is moving forward with its plan to reshape its future in the American healthcare system.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著公司為此轉型做準備，醫療保健產業正密切關注。此舉反映了關於大型醫療保健企業規模與影響力的廣泛全國性辯論。這次拆分是否會為大眾帶來更低的價格與更好的服務仍有待觀察，但顯而易見的是，大型醫療保健集團的時代正面臨新的挑戰。目前，CVS 健康正按計畫推進，以重塑其在美國醫療保健系統中的未來。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To divide something into two or more separate parts.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（裂縫），這裡作動詞用。文中：The company, which is worth $117 billion, plans to split its operations into two separate businesses.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the same building or under the same management/organization.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 在同一個屋簷下（指在同一個機構或管理之下）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思容易理解，但這裡引申為將不同業務整合在同一家公司管理。文中：By bringing insurance, pharmacy benefits, and retail services under one roof, these companies hoped to control more of the market.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To remove the valuable parts of something, often leaving it useless.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「脫掉（衣服）」，這裡指拆解公司資產。文中：A company spokesman had even warned that such a breakup could allow private equity firms to strip the healthcare system for parts.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Negative reaction or resistance to a plan or change.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞片語 push back 演變而來的名詞，指外界對某項政策的阻力。文中：The Guardian Business noted that this political pushback against healthcare giants has been a significant factor in the company's decision.

sources.name: The Guardian Business
sources.title: CVS Health to split pharmacy chain from health insurance

quiz.question: Which specific components will fall under the new CVS Health business entity?

options.A: Retail stores, in-store clinics, and mail-order prescription services.
options.B: Aetna insurance, Caremark pharmacy benefits, and home/primary care services.
options.C: All retail pharmacy operations and the management of Aetna insurance.
options.D: Only the pharmacy benefits manager (Caremark) and retail pharmacy locations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，新的 CVS Health 將負責管理保險公司 Aetna、藥局福利管理商 Caremark，以及針對老年人的居家與初級照護服務。選項 A 描述的是將獨立出來的 CVS Pharmacy 業務；選項 C 將兩者混淆；選項 D 忽略了保險與照護服務，因此皆為錯誤。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the timing and motivation behind CVS Health's decision to split?

options.A: The company decided to split primarily to increase its share price to $44.
options.B: The company chose to split voluntarily to demonstrate its commitment to innovation.
options.C: The split is a strategic reaction to mounting political and regulatory pressures on large healthcare conglomerates.
options.D: The split was mandated by a new federal law passed by Senators Hawley and Warren.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第五段提到政治上的反對力量是該公司決策的重要因素，且第四段提到政府對這類巨型企業的壓力日益增加。選項 A 錯誤，因為 44 美元是股價下跌後的低點而非目標；選項 B 忽略了外部壓力；選項 D 錯誤，因為該法案僅是提出（introduced），並非已經通過的強制法律。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the phrase 'strip the healthcare system for parts' imply?

options.A: To dismantle a company to sell its individual assets for profit.
options.B: To repair the broken components of the healthcare system.
options.C: To reorganize the company to improve efficiency and patient care.
options.D: To remove unnecessary staff to reduce operational costs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。該片語源自汽車拆解業，意指將一個整體拆解成個別零件出售以獲取利潤。在文中，這是公司發言人先前警告若強制拆分公司可能會發生的負面後果。選項 B、C、D 皆未掌握該片語在商業語境中帶有「破壞性變賣資產」的負面含義。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: CVS Health is planning to close all its retail stores by 2028.
options.B: The American healthcare system is failing due to a lack of insurance providers.
options.C: CVS Health is splitting its business as a response to the challenges facing large healthcare conglomerates.
options.D: Government regulators have successfully forced all healthcare companies to lower their prices.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文核心在於探討 CVS Health 宣布拆分業務的決策，並將此舉置於「巨型醫療保健企業時代面臨挑戰」的背景下進行分析。選項 A 與事實不符；選項 B 並非文章主旨；選項 D 過度誇大，文章僅提到政府正在施壓，並未表示價格已成功降低。
